cp1_gateCodeRead.headerName: authorization: "Bearer <ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN value>" -- read directly from config.gateServiceToken, itself env.ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN (services/engine-api/src/config.ts:58). Never guessed.
cp1_gateCodeRead.routesCoveredByBearerCheck: The outer app.use("*", ...) in server.ts runs before ALL routing except an explicit path==="/health"||path==="/ready" bypass. It covers every /v1/* route mounted (site-context, briefing, findings, hydrology, topography, encumbrances, chat, map-layers, document-ingest, property-nodes [parcel-terrain + flood-drainage]) AND the /v1/* catch-all 501 responder -- i.e. literally everything except /health and /ready.
cp1_gateCodeRead.onlyArmedWhenTruthy: The check is `if (config.gateServiceToken) { ... }` -- with ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN unset (current prod state) the block is skipped entirely and only the unsigned, shape-only gate-front headers (parseGateFrontHeaders) gate the request. This matches _inbox/2026-08-27_engine_api_gate_bypass_finding.md (F22) exactly, live-reverified below.
cp1_gateCodeRead.secondLayer_gateContextMode: v1.use("*", ...) separately verifies a signed gate-context (GATE_CONTEXT_SIGNING_KEY) but only in "enforce" mode; default when the signing key is set (it is, live) and GATE_CONTEXT_MODE is unset is "log" (verify+log, never reject). Out of this mission's routes-covered question but relevant: even after ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN is armed, gate-context stays advisory-only unless GATE_CONTEXT_MODE=enforce is also set, which nothing in this mission asks for -- noted, not actioned.

finding_1_cortexApi_not_a_plain_var.claim_in_mission: "cortex-api carries ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN as a plain env var (value unread)"
finding_1_cortexApi_not_a_plain_var.live_evidence: legacy-design-tools-p179-gate/.github/workflows/cloud-run-deploy.yml line 266, the live gcloud run deploy --set-secrets list, already contains `ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN=HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY:latest` and separately `RETRIEVAL_API_KEY=HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY:latest`. cortex-api's ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN is ALREADY a Secret Manager reference -- to the pre-existing secret HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY, not to any not-yet-minted secret. There is no plain var to 'switch.'
finding_1_cortexApi_not_a_plain_var.consequence: cortex-api today sends `Authorization: Bearer <current value of secret HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY>` on every engine-api call. If the engine is armed with a NEW, different ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN value (as the mission's step 2 describes: 'mint ... with one value'), cortex-api's calls will 401 UNLESS cortex-api's deploy is also updated to point at the new secret -- which the mission does plan (PR on legacy-design-tools), so this specific caller is coverable by mission scope, but the premise driving the PR text ('plain env var') is wrong and must not be used to write the PR description or the operator update.

finding_2_smartsiteMcp_already_carries_a.claim_in_mission: "smartsite-mcp carries none and now calls the engine directly (P-152 lane 5)"
finding_2_smartsiteMcp_already_carries_a.live_evidence: legacy-design-tools-p179-gate/.github/workflows/cloud-run-deploy-smartsite-mcp.yml line 166 --set-secrets already contains `HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY=HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY:latest`. artifacts/smartsite-mcp/src/engine-client.ts:43-45 resolves its Bearer token as `process.env.HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY ?? process.env.ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN ?? ""` -- HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY is checked FIRST.
finding_2_smartsiteMcp_already_carries_a.consequence: smartsite-mcp is NOT starved of a credential today; it already sends `Authorization: Bearer <HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY value>`. Adding ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN to its deploy config (as mission step 2 plans) will be INERT at runtime -- the `??` precedence means HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY keeps winning unless that var is also removed from smartsite-mcp's deploy config or the source's precedence is flipped. Neither is in the mission's stated PR scope. Filing the PR as originally worded would ship code that does not do what its description claims.

finding_3_hauska_mcp_server_is_a_live_un.live_evidence: gcloud run services describe hauska-mcp-server --project=hauska-prod-497015 --region=us-central1: SERVING, revision hauska-mcp-server-00092-pur, env includes HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_URL (plain) and HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY (secretRef -> secret HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY). Its client, /p/hauska-mcp-server/src/engine-api-client.ts:58-67, resolves its Bearer as `process.env.HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN ?? process.env.HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY ?? ""` -- it has no HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN, so it currently sends `Authorization: Bearer <HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY value>` to engine-api, per _inbox/2026-08-27_engine_api_gate_bypass_finding.md's own enumeration (four callers named there: hauska-mcp-server, cortex-api, hauska-map/property-explorer, smartcity-dashboards -- this mission's 'what is true today' names only two of the four).
finding_3_hauska_mcp_server_is_a_live_un.consequence: hauska-mcp-server is owned by the substrate seat and is outside both of this mission's two registered worktrees. If ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN is minted as a NEW value distinct from HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY and mounted on the engine, hauska-mcp-server's engine-api calls will start returning 401 with zero PR in this mission touching it. This directly trips the mission's own falsifier #1 ('If a caller loses its reads at any point in the rollout, the order was wrong; roll the engine back first') and is a real production regression for a live, currently-serving MCP surface, not a hypothetical.
